correctness.rationale: Guo's proof explicitly produces a homological eigenvalue \(\rho=\pm\lambda\) and an Alexander root at \(\rho\). The L-space staircase can be paired for every real \(t>1\) into strictly positive differences of \(t^n+t^{-n}\), with the parity-dependent leftover also positive. Hence \(\Delta_K(t)>0\) for \(t>1\), excluding \(\rho=+\lambda\) and forcing \(\rho=-\lambda\). Reciprocity gives the second root \(-\lambda^{-1}\). The argument is symbolic and covers all genera allowed by the source theorem.

value.rationale: The recent theorem is designed as a spectral obstruction for candidate lens-surgery knots. Resolving its remaining sign ambiguity changes the usable test: at the first slope below Baker's threshold a candidate must have a negative Alexander root in \(( -\infty,-1)\), and reciprocity forces the partner root in \((-1,0)\). This is a natural structural sharpening tied to the exact threshold, not an arbitrary specialization, and it links the Floer staircase sign pattern directly to the pseudo-Anosov dilatation eigenvalue.
